parts.watchFor: Ayyub has everything, then loses almost everything. Watch what stays the same.

questions.q: What did Ayyub do with his wealth in the good years?
options: Gave freely to the poor and to travellers

questions.q: Who stayed with Ayyub and cared for him when he was ill?
What happened when Ayyub struck the ground with his foot?
options: A cool spring welled up and healed him

lesson.text: Ayyub was grateful in good times and patient in hard ones, and through both he kept turning back to God. God called him an excellent servant.
lesson.curious: Muslims honour Ayyub, known in the Bible as Job, as a model of patience who never stopped turning back to God.

reflect.muslim: What hardship are you carrying now? Have you told God about it, the way Ayyub did?
reflect.curious: What helps you stay steady when things fall apart?

parts.act: Visit or message someone who is ill or going through a hard time.

parts.watchFor: Madyan's traders cheat. Watch how they answer the prophet who tells them to stop.

options: They gave short measure and short weight

questions.q: What did the people mock Shu'ayb with?
options: Does your prayer tell you how we may run our trade?

questions.q: Where did the people run on the day of burning heat?
options: To the shade of a dark cloud

lesson.text: Shu'ayb taught that faith reaches into business: full measure, fair weight, no cheating. Madyan thought prayer had nothing to do with trade. Honesty at work is part of worship.
lesson.curious: Muslims honour Shu'ayb, often identified with the biblical Jethro, for teaching that honesty in trade is part of faith.

carry.title: Shu'ayb's words of reliance on God

reflect.muslim: Where in your work or studies are you tempted to cut corners? What would full measure look like there?
reflect.curious: Do you think faith should affect how people do business? Why or why not?

parts.act: Be completely honest in one deal, trade or piece of work this week, even where no one would notice.
